display.purpose: Hero h1 only. Uppercase Montserrat 450. The promise before the evidence.

headline.purpose: All section headings. Montserrat 200 — authority without aggression.

body.purpose: All running prose and descriptions. Geist 300. Max 54ch.

label.purpose: Section tags and stat labels only. Uppercase, loose tracking. Categorises, never leads.

display-numeric.purpose: Large statistical figures only. Barlow Condensed italic 700, tabular-nums. Hard numbers at hero scale; used nowhere else.

shadows.name: structural-float
shadows.purpose: Nav on scroll, social FAB, overlays. The only permitted shadow in the system.

motion.name: ease-expo
motion.purpose: Default easing for scroll reveals, nav, and entrance animations.

motion.name: press-in
motion.purpose: Active/press state transition for all buttons. Must feel instant.

narrative.overview:
PayRoll Protect is a financial control mechanism, not a consumer application. Every visual decision reads as institutional rigour — the interface is what stands between a contractor's claim and a payment leaving the account. The visual language communicates: this system does not approve things lightly.

The palette is austere by design. Near-black surfaces (Audit Night) form the operating environment. Montserrat provides architectural, authoritative headings at low weight — the kind of type found on a planning document, not a startup landing page. Geist handles all prose and data with clinical legibility. Lime — the single accent colour — appears only at verified, approved, or actionable moments. It is earned. Seeing lime means something cleared.

Interaction is restrained and professional. Controls recede until needed. There are no animations for decoration. Motion serves comprehension: it reveals verified states, draws attention to discrepancies, and confirms that an action has landed.
keyCharacteristics: Austere dark surfaces — no light mode
Lime reserved for approval and verification only; never decorative
Danger red for unverified, disputed, or flagged states
Low-weight display type (Montserrat 200–450) over dense body copy (Geist 300)
Flat tonal layering with one structural shadow on floating elements
Precision spacing — deliberate rhythm between evidence and action

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Lime is the approval signal. It may not appear on decorative elements, backgrounds, section dividers, or hover states not associated with a verified/approved action. On any given screen, lime should occupy ≤15% of the visible surface.

rules.name: The Binary Verdict Rule
rules.body: Red and lime do not share a visual field at the same hierarchy. When red appears (unverified claim), lime recedes. The visual system enforces a binary outcome — verified or not.

rules.name: The Weight Separation Rule
rules.body: Display and Headline use Montserrat at 200–450. Body and Label use Geist at 300. Never use Montserrat below 18px and never use it for running prose.

rules.name: The Negative Tracking Rule
rules.body: All Montserrat headings carry negative letter-spacing (-0.025em minimum). Positive tracking on display type is prohibited.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Static surfaces carry no box-shadow. Cards are defined by background color and a 1px border. The structural float shadow is reserved for elements that actually leave the document flow.

dos: Do use lime (oklch(0.770 0.206 151)) only on verified, approved, and actionable states.
Do use negative letter-spacing on all Montserrat headings (-0.025em minimum).
Do keep section-opening padding to exactly two tiers: clamp(5rem, 10vw, 8rem) standard, clamp(7rem, 14vw, 10.5rem) hero-scale.
Do use the tonal stack (audit-night → surface → border) for depth. Three steps only.
Do give all interactive elements touch-action: manipulation and :active { transform: scale(0.97); transition: 80ms }.
Do use SVG geometry icons at 18px, 1.4–1.5px stroke-weight, authored consistently.
donts: Don't use lime decoratively — no lime dividers, backgrounds, section accents, or hover treatments unrelated to approval states.
Don't apply translateY(-Xpx) on button hover. Position change is reserved for the active/press state only.
Don't use gradient text or colored border-left on cards, list items, or callouts.
Don't place an eyebrow/kicker label above a section heading.
Don't add box-shadow to static card surfaces.
Don't use Montserrat for body copy or at sizes below 18px.
Don't combine lime and danger red in the same visual field at the same hierarchy level.
